source.note: hand-written; a Rust CLI on Windows, with a shell-startup gotcha

units.text: Starting the Rust rewrite of the token-saver CLI. I'm on Windows, so that's the primary target; Linux and mac can come later. Argument parsing: clap derive or hand-rolled?

For context, clap's two styles: the builder API constructs the parser imperatively and is more flexible at runtime, while the derive API generates the parser from a struct with attributes and gives you typed fields, help text from doc comments, and compile-time checking of the schema. Hand-rolled parsing is only worth it for one or two flags. For a CLI with subcommands, derive is the usual choice.
Derive. I'd rather have the typed struct than save a dependency.
Set up with `clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive"] }` and a `Cli` struct with `Proxy` and `Gain` subcommands. Builds on stable 1.88.
The proxy subcommand runs the wrapped command through the shell. It feels slow, like a full second before anything happens.

Measured it: spawning `powershell -Command` costs about 1.9 seconds on your machine before the wrapped command even starts, because PowerShell loads the user profile (yours imports oh-my-posh and two modules). With `-NoProfile` the spawn drops to about 180 ms. `cmd /C` is around 40 ms but mangles quoting for anything with spaces or unicode. I switched the proxy to `powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command` and the end-to-end `rtk proxy git status` is now 0.3 s instead of 2.1 s.
Great, that's the fix. Note it in the code so I don't 'clean it up' later.
Added a comment above the spawn explaining the 1.9 s profile load and why -NoProfile stays.

expected.content: The user's Rust token-saver CLI targets Windows first; Linux and macOS come later.
The CLI uses clap's derive API for argument parsing because the user prefers the typed struct over saving a dependency.
Spawning PowerShell for the proxy subcommand must use -NoProfile: the user's profile (oh-my-posh and two modules) adds about 1.9 seconds per spawn, versus about 180 ms without it.
